content:
Hi everyone!

AI tools for Lean have changed a lot this past year, and I'm curious how people here actually feel about them: what works, what doesn't, and why some of us skip them entirely.

So here's a quick, informal survey (about 2 minutes) as a series of polls below. A few notes:

• Non-users are just as welcome! There's a poll specifically for you, and those answers are just as interesting.
• Vote for as many options as apply, and add your own if something's missing.
• No right or wrong answers. This isn't about promoting or criticizing any tool.

I'll post a short summary of the results in this thread in a couple of weeks. Thanks for taking part!

/poll How would you describe your Lean experience?
Beginner (< 6 months)
Intermediate (comfortable with tactics, some Mathlib contributions or projects)
Experienced (regular Mathlib/large-project contributor)
Lean core / tooling developer

/poll Which AI tools do you use for Lean? (pick all that apply)
General chat assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, ...)
Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor agent, ...)
In-editor completion (Copilot, LLMLean, Lean Copilot, ...)
Dedicated provers (Aristotle, AlphaProof, DeepSeek-Prover, Kimina, ...)
Lemma search (LeanSearch, Moogle, Loogle + LLM, ...)
Custom/in-house models or scripts

/poll What do you use AI for? (pick all that apply)
Closing individual goals / tactic suggestions
Writing whole proofs from a statement
Autoformalization: informal math → Lean statements
Finding Mathlib lemmas and definitions
Fixing errors / version migration (bumping Lean or Mathlib)
Refactoring, golfing, docstrings, boilerplate
Learning Lean / understanding existing code
Formalizing whole papers or large projects

/poll Overall, how much do AI tools speed up your formalization work?
A lot (2x or more)
Noticeably
Slightly
No net effect
They slow me down

/poll What are the biggest problems you hit? (pick all that apply)
Hallucinated lemma names / nonexistent API
Outdated Lean 3 or old-Mathlib syntax
Proofs that compile but are ugly or fragile
Wrong or subtly mis-stated formalizations
Too slow or too expensive
Hard to integrate into my workflow
Not much, it works well
Open question: what's one workflow or trick that's worked really well for you, or one thing you wish AI tools did better? Reply below :point_down:

/poll If you don't use AI tools for Lean (or stopped), why not? (pick all that apply)
Output quality isn't good enough (wrong lemmas, broken proofs)
Faster to write it myself
I want to understand and learn the proofs myself
Doing the proofs is the fun part for me
Concerns about subtly wrong statements or formalizations
Policy concerns (e.g. Mathlib/project rules on AI-generated code)
Cost or access (paid tools, rate limits, institutional restrictions)
Privacy or licensing concerns
Ethical or environmental concerns
Haven't gotten around to trying it / don't know where to start
